solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: The number for today’s 45?

blocks.note: surface reading: a numerical figure that belongs to whatever entry 45 is
setter's reading: a number is a song, the one sung to 45-down, which turned ninety on this puzzle's date

explanation.walkthrough: 45-down is the Times Crossword, first published in February 1930, so this jumbo marked its ninetieth birthday. 'Number' tempts you towards a figure such as 90, but it means a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional song sung at every birthday party is the musical piece you would perform for the crossword's anniversary.

clue.text: Gases with unpleasant smell in flat

blocks.note: H and O are the chemical symbols for hydrogen and oxygen, two gases
a hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Gas leaking into an apartment leaves a nasty smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but it is the definition in its sense of dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexciting and routine can be called flat or lacking sparkle, which is just what the bored interjection describes.

clue.text: Revolutionary poser with unknown values being tried for Brain-teasers’ World

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: a model poses for an artist or photographer
in algebra unknowns are x, y and z, so two of them can be ZZ
someone up before the magistrates is being tried

explanation.surface: A rebel puzzle-setter with algebraic unknowns is put on trial in the world of brain-teasers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' tempts as a puzzle, a fitting thought here, but it is a person who poses. Up, as in up in court, means on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -dom marks a realm, as in kingdom, so this coinage names the whole realm of puzzles and riddles.

clue.text: Bag for yellow sock lay abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned behaviour is wild and unrestrained, so these letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a bag to hold a yellow sock that was left lying around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' is a noun here: the yellow of an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: In an egg or embryo this membrane pouch holds the yellow nutrient part that feeds the developing young.

clue.text: Fateful day when leader’s abandoned pair flanking demo?

indicators.note: when the leader is abandoned the front of the phrase is left behind, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: the two things either side of something are its sides
a demonstration is a protest march

explanation.surface: A protest turns fateful when its leader deserts and two marchers stand either side.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for the edges of a protest march loses its opening S.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the fifteenth of the third month, so that date is proverbially ominous.

clue.text: What could be long under end of snout

definitions.text: What could be long under end of snout

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
in a down entry, under means placed below, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Something that might grow long just below the tip of the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a moustache sits under the nose and can be grown long. Tache is British slang for moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair grown on the upper lip sits directly beneath the nose, and some people cultivate it at great length.

clue.text: Tirade sent up charity race

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: aid is charitable help
a race of people can be called a tribe

explanation.surface: A rant mocking a charity fun run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' reads as mocked, but in a down clue it turns the word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a long, angry speech of bitter criticism, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Regularly sampled syrup: my, that’s tasty!

indicators.note: sampling at regular intervals takes every other letter rather than all of them

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone tastes syrup and exclaims at how good it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like part of the exclamation, but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The childlike exclamation expresses delight at delicious food, the same reaction as calling something tasty.

clue.text: What solver may refer to when looking up identical medical conditions

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word looking up faces the top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the Oxford English Dictionary, a reference a crossword solver might consult
identical things are the same

explanation.surface: A crossword solver checks a dictionary when looking up two conditions that seem the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' sounds like consulting a reference book; it also turns a word upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An oedema is swelling caused by fluid in body tissue, so the plural names several such ailments.

clue.text: Many Times newspaper plugs unsettled one

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed from its place, so these letters are rearranged
a plug is pushed into a hole, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Many a Times newspaper advertises one that is unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' tempts as the newspaper, but 'Many Times' is the definition and the paper is the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening frequently, on numerous occasions, happens many times.

clue.text: Ninety-ton load originally transported with great diligence

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so only the first letters are taken
transported goods are moved about, so these letters are carried into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of ton
the opening letter of load

explanation.surface: A huge ninety-ton load is moved with careful effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ninety-ton' looks like a single weight, but 'Ninety' is fodder and only the T of ton is used. Ninety nods to the crossword's ninetieth birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with fixed, focused attention and determination means doing it diligently and with concentration.

clue.text: Locals show up in nanoseconds!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: ns is the scientific abbreviation for nanoseconds
Evita is a Lloyd Webber stage musical

explanation.surface: Locals turn up in no time at all!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show up' reads as appear; it splits into a theatre show and an upward turn.
explanation.definitionFit: People born in a place, as opposed to visitors, are its natives or local inhabitants.

clue.text: A case perhaps for charging, out of old tax, interest on deposit

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: ex is Latin for out of
cess is an old word for a local tax
your bag is your thing, your particular interest
a gage is a pledge left as security

explanation.surface: A legal case about charging interest on a deposit after an old tax is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' tempts as a lawsuit about money; it is a suitcase, and 'charging' means an airline's fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlines charge extra for luggage over the free allowance, so an overweight suitcase is a thing they bill for.

clue.text: Is to cease manufacturing warm coats for mothers-to-be?

indicators.note: manufacturing makes something new out of raw material, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clothing firm stops making warm coats for pregnant women.
explanation.walkthrough: In British homes whoever pours the tea is called 'mother' ('shall I be mother?'), so a teapot waiting to be poured is a mother-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: These padded knitted covers keep a teapot hot, and the pot is what the person playing mother will pour from.

clue.text: 1930 for Chinese show in Birmingham with parts exchanged ...

indicators.note: exchanging the parts swaps the positions of the words, rearranging the phrase

blocks.note: the Horse of the Year Show is an equestrian event held at the NEC in Birmingham

explanation.surface: A Chinese performance in Birmingham with its acts swapped round, set in 1930.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last words of the show's name trade places. 1930, the year the Times Crossword began, was a Horse year in the Chinese zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese zodiac assigns each year an animal, and the year starting in early 1930 belonged to the horse.

clue.text: ... This year keen for some cricket?

blocks.note: a third meaning: 2020, the year this puzzle appeared
second meaning: perfect eyesight is called 20/20 vision, so keen-sighted
third meaning: a short form of cricket with twenty overs per side

explanation.surface: This year someone is keen on playing a bit of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 14-down's year theme. Twenty20 is a fast, short cricket format of twenty overs a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal sharp eyesight is measured as twenty-twenty, and the short-format cricket game is named for its twenty overs.

clue.text: Miss, perhaps, loch, with fog to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry west is the left side, so that piece is placed first

blocks.note: fog is a kind of haze
L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake shrouded in mist, with a young woman nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss, perhaps' means a girl, and the answer is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A young unmarried woman is addressed as Miss, and this is one example of a girl's first name.

clue.text: Came out with partner once requested?

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to claim something is to request it as your due

explanation.surface: Someone came out as gay alongside a former partner, as had been requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came out with' suggests leaving with a companion; it means blurted out.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out with a remark is to say it suddenly, which is to cry out or utter it.

clue.text: Drag couple, pushing wife back

indicators.note: pushing a letter out of its place takes it away from there before it is set down again
putting something at the back means it is placed last, after the rest

blocks.note: a couple is two
w is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A couple drag along, the husband shoving his wife backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The W of the number word moves from the middle to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a vehicle or boat along behind you with a rope is both to drag and to haul it.

clue.text: Carbon copy perfectly covers a composition

indicators.note: a cover goes around what it protects, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to a T means perfectly
cc is the abbreviation for carbon copy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exact carbon copy hides a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfectly' gives the three-word phrase to a T, which opens up to take the copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a piece of keyboard music, usually fast and showy, so it is a musical composition.

clue.text: Times cryptic has bagged large one

definitions.text: Times cryptic has bagged large one

indicators.note: something cryptic is mysterious and scrambled, so these letters are jumbled
to bag something is to put it in a bag, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Times crossword has scored a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the Times Crossword reaching ninety is a large one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A significant anniversary or achievement marks a stage, like a stone by the road counting miles.

clue.text: Piano master given one month by notorious landlord

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: Peter Rachman was an infamous slum landlord in 1950s London
the Roman numeral for one
Nov is the calendar abbreviation for November

explanation.surface: A great pianist receives one month's notice from a notorious landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachman's name became a British byword for exploiting tenants, giving English the word Rachmanism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian composer was also one of the greatest concert pianists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Insensitive request for a ring — receiving different sort

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a ring is a phone call, so asking for one is saying 'call us'
a ring of a different sort: the round letter O

explanation.surface: A tactless request for a wedding ring gets a different kind entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' is first a phone call and then, in 'different sort', a circle shaped like O.
explanation.definitionFit: A callous person is hardened and unfeeling towards others, showing no sensitivity or sympathy.

clue.text: See, in singular working method, way to extend playtime

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: s is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
lo is an old word for look or see
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A teacher finds a peculiar method of making playtime last longer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo goes between the S and the MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow-motion replays stretch a moment of sporting play so it takes longer to watch.

clue.text: Flash detective with Latin touch

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'in a flash'
DI is a Detective Inspector
cum is the Latin word for with

explanation.surface: A showy detective with a deft Latin flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' tempts as an adjective for the detective, but it is a moment; 'touch' is a noun, a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch of something is a small quantity of it, just as a modicum is a little bit.

clue.text: Host nabbing posh family to help out

indicators.note: to nab is to grab and hold, so one piece is caught inside another

blocks.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
U means upper-class, as in 'U and non-U' British usage
your kin are your family

explanation.surface: A host grabs a well-to-do family to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from a 1950s British debate about posh and non-posh word choices.
explanation.definitionFit: To muck in is a British idiom for pitching in and sharing the work, lending a hand to others.

clue.text: In short, why you can’t ring chemist

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: you cannot ring if there is no bell

explanation.surface: Briefly, the reason you can't phone the pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chemist' tempts as a British pharmacy, but it is the Swedish scientist. 'Ring' is ringing a doorbell, not phoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, who invented dynamite and founded the prizes, was a Swedish chemist by profession.

clue.text: Overheard refusals to touch kid’s hankie

indicators.note: what is overheard reaches you by ear, so the word is judged by its sound
pieces that touch sit right against each other, so they are joined end to end

blocks.note: noes are refusals, said the same as the body part
to kid and to rag both mean to tease

explanation.surface: A child's refusals are overheard when you go near their handkerchief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' tempts as a child, but it is a verb meaning tease; rag is British for tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang name for a handkerchief describes it as a cloth for wiping the nose.

clue.text: Forward social security packs for one

indicators.note: packing puts things inside a case, so one piece is filled in

blocks.note: say means for example, for one
SS is the abbreviation for social security

explanation.surface: A forward-thinking welfare system packs in one claimant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a direction; it means cheeky. 'For one' gives a word meaning for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is bold and cheeky in manner, which is what sassy, lively and impudent, describes.

clue.text: Only be doing this having put away volume

indicators.note: something put away is taken out of sight, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: what you, the solver, should be doing with this clue
v is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: Just get on with this once you have put the book back on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks to you: what you should be doing to this clue is solving it, minus the V.
explanation.definitionFit: A sole survivor is the only one, so the adjective means single or one and no other.

clue.text: Advance payments: one way to get by

blocks.note: a sub is a payment in advance of wages
the Roman numeral for one
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Getting paid early is one way to make ends meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way' reads as a phrase, but each word gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is to manage to stay alive on little, which is exactly what subsisting means.

clue.text: “Meet in Colorado” — I like this clue!

blocks.note: CO is the US postal abbreviation for Colorado
I and me both refer to the speaker
this clue is an across entry, so it is like one

explanation.surface: A setter quotes a slogan inviting people to meet up in Colorado, and admires the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I like this clue' sounds like praise, but splits into a pronoun and the clue's own direction in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone is to meet or encounter them, often by chance.

clue.text: Crawling out, mostly quiet

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: someone out is away from home
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A baby crawling about, mostly silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawling' looks like moving on hands and knees, but means swarming, as in 'crawling with'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place crawling with something is full of it, just as a place awash with it is flooded by it.

clue.text: Running to ground, maybe, voracious predator turning on swallow

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards
in an across entry, a piece placed on another goes after it

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
the wolf is a famously hungry predator

explanation.surface: A hungry predator chases its prey to ground and turns on a swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running to ground' sounds like a hunt; it describes liquid moving downward. 'Swallow' tempts as the bird, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that runs downward towards the earth is a flow heading down, so it describes a descending current.

clue.text: Feeds small numbers at college, in High School

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: nos is a short form of numbers
HS is the abbreviation for High School
a British student up at university is attending college

explanation.surface: A canteen serves small portions to college students at a high school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small numbers' reads as few people; it is the abbreviated form. A nosh-up is British slang for a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A feed is informal for a hearty meal, and a nosh-up is a British slang term for one.

clue.text: Grand performance's finale for circus clown

indicators.note: a finale comes at the very end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: august means grand and dignified
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A circus clown takes part in a grand finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like a describing word for the performance, but it is a piece in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: The auguste is the classic clumsy red-nosed clown type, the foil to the elegant whiteface clown.

clue.text: The last word? Just what one needs? Yes, primarily

definitions.text: The last word? Just what one needs? Yes, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
'that's it!' says something is exactly what was wanted
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A string of eager questions about whether something is ideal, ending in a firm yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Each question gives a piece, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a facility that is just what one needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a useful or pleasant facility, a feature that provides comfort or convenience when needed.

clue.text: A game for the 45's birthday party?

blocks.note: 45-down is the Times Crossword, and what it is made of is a clue
a do is a party, here held for a birthday

explanation.surface: A board game suggested for the crossword's birthday celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo, sold as Clue in North America, is the murder-mystery board game; a do is British for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluedo is a board game in which players deduce the murderer, weapon and room.

clue.text: Cricket team after hotel

blocks.note: first meaning: a national side in international cricket
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the code word for I follows the one for H

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team checking out of its hotel; the second definition uses the radio spelling alphabet, where Hotel stands for H.
explanation.definitionFit: The country fields a top cricket side, and its name is the radio code word for the letter following H.

clue.text: There are stories from Welshman appearing in The Times etc

blocks.note: Dai is a stock Welsh first name
stories can be untruths, fibs

explanation.surface: Stories by a Welsh writer are published in The Times and other papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stories' suggests newspaper articles, fitting the surface, but means fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times and similar papers published every day are daily newspapers, called dailies for short.

clue.text: Hard test occurring at regular intervals

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A difficult exam that keeps coming round at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular intervals' is vaguer than the answer, which strictly means hourly.
explanation.definitionFit: Horal means relating to hours or happening every hour, so it happens at a regular interval.

clue.text: Children’s doctor lacking energy to work out

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: Dr Seuss wrote The Cat in the Hat and other children's books
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A paediatrician too tired to exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children's doctor' suggests a paediatrician; it is the pen name of the author. 'Work out' tempts as exercise, but means figure out.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something out is British slang for figuring it out or realising the truth about it.

clue.text: Touching, moving letters from dog trainer

indicators.note: if the letters move around, the phrase is spelt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A moving letter of thanks from the person who trained the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' and 'moving' both suggest emotion; the first is the definition, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching as a preposition means concerning or about, which is what this phrase also means.

clue.text: Derby game involves four sort of shooting

indicators.note: a game leg is a lame, crooked one, so these letters are knocked out of shape
to involve is to enfold, so one piece is wrapped inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A local derby football match where four people are involved in a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby game' reads as a local football match, but 'game' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-by is a shooting carried out from a moving vehicle as it passes the target.

clue.text: Hot, wearing kit attached to mat — it’s 90 degrees!

indicators.note: whoever wears clothing is inside it, so one piece sits within the others
things attached are joined together, so the pieces are placed side by side

blocks.note: a rig is a set of gear or kit
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
matted hair is in a tangle

explanation.surface: A sweaty gym-goer in kit on a mat in ninety-degree heat.
explanation.walkthrough: '90 degrees' sounds like the temperature in Fahrenheit, but means the angle. Ninety again nods to the crossword's birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle of ninety degrees, a quarter turn as at the corner of a square, is a right angle.

clue.text: In turning up sibyl, a monastery’s deviant

definitions.note: used as a noun: something that deviates from the norm

indicators.note: the letters are in the words themselves, sitting inside the phrase
in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A prophetess turning up at a monastery is out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: A sibyl is a prophetess of ancient legend, which makes a fine distraction here.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something that departs from the normal pattern, a deviation or irregular case.

clue.text: Extravagant Times clue for Einstein?

indicators.note: the answer is itself a cryptic clue for the given word, so read the other way it rearranges into it

blocks.note: taken as written; its letters rearrange into a word in the answer
the first word of the answer is a setter's signal to rearrange, completing the clue

explanation.surface: A lavish era of the Times: what would be a clue to the physicist?
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: 'naughty nineties' would itself be a clue for EINSTEIN, with naughty telling you to rearrange NINETIES. The Times Crossword is now in its nineties.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1890s in Britain were remembered as a decade of frivolity and loose morals, a period of extravagant living.

clue.text: Less likely to spot one putting on one’s coat?

definitions.text: Less likely to spot one putting on one’s coat?

blocks.clueFragment: Less likely to spot one putting on one’s coat?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone less likely to notice a person pulling on an overcoat
setter's reading: paint less likely to leave spots on the decorator applying a coat of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' is a layer of paint and 'spot' means splash, so the clue describes a thick paint that does not run.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint sold with this label is a thick gel that will not run or splatter as it is brushed on.

clue.text: Removed from board, sulked

blocks.note: first meaning: in draughts, a piece is taken off the board as a penalty when its player misses a capture
second meaning: went into a fit of pique

explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed from board' sounds like someone sacked from a company board, which pairs nicely with sulking; it is really a draughts move.
explanation.definitionFit: In draughts (checkers) an opponent's piece is forfeited this way, and being in a huff means showing petulant annoyance.

clue.text: This enigmatic item's put out along with news

indicators.note: something enigmatic is a puzzle to be unscrambled, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive S included
someone put out is annoyed, cross
word is news, as in 'any word from them?'

explanation.surface: This mysterious feature is published alongside the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' tempts as published, and 'This' is the definition: the very puzzle you are solving, whose ninetieth birthday it celebrates.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points at itself: you are holding a puzzle from the London newspaper's long-running cryptic series.

clue.text: Some of our best, and biggest, friends win dosh and flourish, unexpectedly

definitions.text: Some of our best, and biggest, friends

indicators.note: what happens unexpectedly breaks the expected order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some of our closest friends win a pile of cash and thrive against the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog is man's best friend, and this breed is the tallest of all. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs are proverbially our best friends, and this giant hunting breed is the tallest dog there is.

clue.text: 1930, where fifty percent of history is still

blocks.note: history is the past, and fifty percent is half
the 's contraction of is
still and even both intensify a comparison: still better, even better

explanation.surface: In 1930, half of history was still to come.
explanation.walkthrough: '1930' looks like the founding year of the Times Crossword again, but here it is a time on the 24-hour clock.
explanation.definitionFit: On a 24-hour clock 19:30 is seven thirty in the evening, read as thirty minutes after seven.

clue.text: Base bachelor quite keen for 90-minute affair

blocks.note: the foot of something is its base
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
all and quite both mean completely, as in 'all alone'
someone game for anything is keen

explanation.surface: A low-minded single man rather keen on a ninety-minute fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' suggests romance, set up by bachelor and keen, but it is just an event. Ninety again marks the crossword's birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer match lasts ninety minutes of playing time, so it is a ninety-minute event.

clue.text: Singles that are old: at least 90

blocks.note: first meaning: vinyl singles played at 45 revolutions per minute, now old technology
second meaning: more than one of the number 45 adds up to 90 or more

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singles that are old' sounds like elderly unmarried people, fitting 'at least 90'. Puzzle 45 is the Times Crossword, ninety this year.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl singles spun at forty-five rpm, and two or more copies of the number forty-five total at least ninety.

clue.text: Disturbances after polling bringing change in Russia

indicators.note: to poll a tree or animal is to cut off its top, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: troubles are disturbances or unrest

clue.text: Ticked over five hundred large — that is five hundred— boxes!

clue.text: What solvers are keen to fill? Not quite keen, on reflection

explanation.definitionFit: The pattern of squares in a crossword is what solvers want to complete with answers.

clue.text: Might the setters pull a fast one?

definitions.text: Might the setters pull a fast one?

clue.text: Live outside Rugby by backward out-of-town area

clue.text: Stick with this game — a version you’re still saddled with?

blocks.clueFragment: Stick with this game — a version you’re still saddled with?

clue.text: Film for setter?
